title: HTTP Header Hunt
subtitle: Harden the Nimbus Freight customer portal
summary: The Nimbus Freight portal is shipping responses with almost no browser security controls, and a build token is leaking in a response header. Audit the live service, then apply a hardened header policy and prove the fix.
scenario: You are a security engineer on the Nimbus Freight platform team. A penetration test flagged that the customer portal sends unprotected responses and leaks internal build metadata. The deployment tooling opens a small authenticated admin API so you can apply a reviewed header policy without redeploying. Your job: hunt the leak, harden the edge, and record evidence.
prerequisites: Comfort reading raw HTTP with curl
learningObjectives: Inspect real HTTP responses and identify missing browser security headers
Explain the risk of clickjacking, MIME sniffing and insecure transport policy
Apply a validated Content-Security-Policy, HSTS and related headers through an admin API
Verify remediation against the live service and document evidence
authorizedScope: Only the Nimbus Freight portal running inside this lab session (CF_TARGET_URL, 127.0.0.1 inside the workspace). No other hosts are in scope and outbound network access is denied by the session policy.
riskSummary: Missing browser security headers allow clickjacking, MIME-confusion attacks and downgrade/credential-leak scenarios. A leaked build token can enable artifact tampering if the build system trusts it.
remediation: Apply a CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', enforce HSTS with a one-year max-age on all responses, set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, a strict Referrer-Policy, and a restrictive Permissions-Policy. Remove build metadata from production response headers and keep tokens out of transport headers.
conclusion: You audited a live application, found a real leaked build token, and remediated the missing security headers by driving a validated admin API. This is the same workflow used to roll out edge policies safely in production.

objectives.title: Find the leaked build token
objectives.description: Authenticate to the portal with the demo account from your briefing, then inspect an authenticated response. A build token is leaking in a response header. Submit it as a flag (format CF{...}).

hints.text: Start with the briefing: the demo credentials are in ~/credentials.txt. Log in with curl and keep the session cookie.
Use `curl -sD - -b cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8080/dashboard -o /dev/null` to read the full response headers.

objectives.title: Apply a hardened header policy
objectives.description: Use labctl to apply a policy JSON that adds the required security headers to every response. The platform verifies the live responses, not your intent.
objectives.evidencePrompt: The platform will fetch /, /login and /dashboard and validate CSP, HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and frame protection.

validation.criteria: All three pages return CSP (frame-ancestors 'none', no unsafe script sources), HSTS max-age >= 15552000, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and X-Frame-Options: DENY

hints.text: `labctl audit` reports how the live service scores against the required header set.
Policy shape: {"headers":{"Content-Security-Policy":"default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; ..."}}. Start from `labctl policy show`.
Apply with `labctl policy apply hardened.json`, then re-check with `curl -sI http://127.0.0.1:8080/`.

objectives.title: Document the finding and fix
objectives.description: Write ~/evidence/headers-findings.json with the missing headers you observed and the headers you applied. The validator compares your evidence against the live service.

validation.criteria: Evidence file exists, lists at least four previously missing headers, and the applied values match live responses

hints.text: Create it with jq or python3: `python3 - <<'PY'` ... `PY` — then run the objective check.

walkthrough.title: Read the briefing
walkthrough.body: The briefing lists the portal URL, the demo account and the admin tool available in this workspace.

walkthrough.title: Inspect the current headers
walkthrough.body: Unauthenticated responses are missing every browser security control.

walkthrough.title: Log in and find the leaked token
walkthrough.body: The authenticated dashboard leaks build metadata in a response header.
walkthrough.snippet: curl -s -c cookies.txt -d 'email=ops@nimbusfreight.example&password=freight2024' http://127.0.0.1:8080/login -o /dev/null && curl -sD - -b cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8080/dashboard -o /dev/null

walkthrough.title: Submit the flag
walkthrough.body: Copy the CF{...} value from the X-Build-Token header into the objective panel.

walkthrough.title: Draft the hardened policy
walkthrough.body: Start from the active policy and add the six required headers.

walkthrough.title: Apply and verify
walkthrough.body: Apply the policy through the authenticated admin API, then re-fetch the pages. The target applies it in-memory immediately.
walkthrough.snippet: labctl policy apply hardened.json && curl -sD - http://127.0.0.1:8080/ -o /dev/null

walkthrough.title: Write evidence
walkthrough.body: Record which headers were missing and the exact values you applied, then run the evidence objective.

tests.description: Portal responds on the private network
Build token is only exposed on an authenticated response
Target process and session mounts are removed on stop
